reason: Feasibility is fine: it is a read-only tool tweak, R8 does not apply and nothing reaches the finals. The value is close to zero, and part of the claim is wrong. (1) The finding says scoreDescending sorts by public score. It actually sorts by the kernel's BEST score across versions. amanatar/optimized-biohub-max-score is #2 while its page shows 'Public Score 0.910' and 'Best Score 0.953 V4' (round10/scan_browser.notes.md l.14). P4b(c) needs the LATEST version's score, so 'above x138' does not mean what a port needs. (2) The #1 kernel (HF v3) is itself 0.953, and so are all of the top 4. 'New at #1' or 'above x138' therefore only means best >= 0.953 (ties). It cannot tell a 0.953 copy from the 0.954-0.955 hole or from the >= 0.956 port bar, so it is not a trigger or a P2-strength signal. (3) It lags. A re-run keeps its old position while it is RUNNING or unscored (~7 h), and the existing P2 dateRun clause (CONTEXT l.2140) already fires hours earlier on any new or re-run kernel. (4) It is redundant. diff_kernels (tools/e10_snapshot.py l.458-475) already prints 'NEW <ref> pos j' and 'LASTRUN ... pos i -> j' for the scoreDescending list. Agents already read the position against x138 by hand (round10 scan_plancheck/scan_hypotheses). (5) The exact score still needs the page, because kernels_list has no score field. The one sound use is negative triage: a scored kernel strictly below x138 has best <= 0.953, so it is no port and not in the hole. That saves at most one browser look in a scenario with a 5-10% prior.
fix: Optional and not needed. If it is done anyway, add an info-only line (not counted in CHANGES) to the comp_scoreDescending diff. It gives each NEW or moved ref's position relative to the x138 ref and says: 'sort key = BEST score over versions; above x138 => best >= 0.953 (ties at 0.953 are uninformative, not a trigger); strictly below x138 => best <= 0.953 => no port / not in the 0.954-0.955 hole; a RUNNING re-run keeps its old position; the exact latest-version score needs the page (P4b(c), P4c(7))'. Add one unit test in tests/test_e10_snapshot.py covering above/below/x138-missing. Do not add it to the P2 rule text.
realistic_gain: 0 on public/private LB. Operationally it could save at most one browser page read in the successor scenario (prior ~5-10%). It carries a small risk of being misread as a >= 0.954 trigger if it is worded as 'score >= 0.953'.
